newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trade was steady to weak on moderate demand and mostly moderate offerings on Choice product, and moderate to heavy offerings on Select product, USDA said.

Retail and HRI demand was for immediate needs, while forward interests were rather light. Chuck and round cuts trended lower throughout the week as processors were forced to control inventories on some of these cuts.

Loin cuts traded rather uneven but ended the trading period on a weak note. Trade on rib cuts was generally steady with a firm undertone on the Select product as these cuts were seen as better values.

Closely trimmed product traded uneven on moderate demand as the Choice cuts were generally steady, while the Select cuts traded lower. Reduced slaughter, coupled with increased supplies of Select product, stimulated trade on beef trimmings to sharply higher price levels at the end of the trading period on moderate demand and light offerings.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on light to moderate demand and offerings, however, a firm undertone was noted on the fed cattle grinds.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal generally steady; Select and Choice chuck primal 1.00 to 4.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal 2.00 to 3.50 lower; Select and Choice loin primal steady to 2.00 lower; Closely trimmed items steady to 2.50 lower; Beef trimmings 6.50 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally steady.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn .37 at 105.68; 700/850 Dn .49 at 104.03; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 2.25 at 98.77; 700/850 Dn 1.58 at 97.81.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The boneless beef market rebounded this week after recent declines. Boneless beef traded higher during this trading period as offerings were light due to the reductions in the slaughter numbers the past week.

Demand was moderate to good from retail grinders early in the week and increased demand was also seen from fast food grinders as the week progressed. The cow carcass complex traded steady on moderate demand and light to moderate offerings. Moreover, cow cuts traded uneven, with the tenderloins at lower price due to seasonal light demand.

Utility carcasses steady; Cutter steady; Fresh 90% boneless beef 3.00-4.00 higher; 85% 2.00-4.00 higher; 75% 2.00-2.50 higher; 65% 1.00-1.50 higher. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, September 26, 1996 was estimated at 65.45 per cwt., up 2.02 from a week ago Friday.
